factionId Integer Unique ID of the owning faction (0: Neutral, 1: Player, 2+: AI/Enemy).
opacity Double The current alpha value of the cell (used for fade-in animations).
isDirty Boolean Flag indicating if the cell's visual state needs a re-render.
lastCapturedAt Timestamp ISO8601 string of when the ownership last changed.

2. Game State

The UI state manages the visibility and theme of the overlays during the active session.

Variable Type Description
isOverlayEnabled Boolean Global toggle for the 'Scouting Mode' (Hotkeys 'V').
activeFactions List List of faction IDs currently present in the viewport.
factionColorMap Map<Int, String> Mapping of faction IDs to Hex Color strings (e.g., 1: "#0000FF").
selectedCellId String The ID of the cell the player is currently inside.
transitionQueue List Queue of Cell IDs currently undergoing capture animations.

3. API / Local Repository Interface

Since the MVP focuses on local persistence (Hive DB), these methods define the interface between the Territory Manager and the Mapbox Controller.

Method Parameters Return Type Description
getCellsInBounds BoundingBox List Fetches all conquered cells within the current map camera view.
updateCellOwnership cellId, factionId Void Updates Hive DB and triggers a visual refresh for a specific cell.
getFactionTheme factionId ThemeObject Returns the primary and secondary (border) colors for a faction.

4. Key Components

  • TerritoryLayerManager: The primary controller that interacts with Mapbox GL. It manages three distinct Mapbox layers: fill (for the 30% tint), line (for the 2px borders), and symbol (for optional faction icons).
  • S2BoundaryService: A utility class that converts S2 cell tokens into GeoJSON Polygons. It calculates the four corner coordinates for each S2 Level 15 cell.
  • ContiguousBoundaryEngine: A logic module that performs a "union" or "edge-filtering" operation. It determines which cell edges are shared by the same faction to suppress internal borders, creating the "blob" effect.
  • AnimationController: A lightweight tween engine that handles the 500ms opacity fade-in and the "border pulse" effect using a Ticker or Mapbox's setPaintProperty transition.

5. Logic Flow

A. Rendering the "Blob" Territory

To ensure contiguous territories look like a single shape (User Story 3):

  1. Query the local database for all cells in the viewport grouped by factionId.
  2. For each faction, generate a GeoJSON FeatureCollection.
  3. Edge Filtering Algorithm:
    • For every cell in the faction, identify its four S2 neighbors.
    • If a neighbor belongs to the same faction, mark that specific edge as "Internal."
    • If a neighbor belongs to a different faction or is neutral, mark that edge as "Boundary."
  4. Render the "Boundary" edges as a LineLayer with 2px width and 100% opacity.
  5. Render the interior area as a FillLayer with 30% opacity.

B. Real-time Capture Feedback (User Story 2)

When a cell conquest is triggered:

  1. Update the factionId in the local Hive DB.
  2. Trigger the AnimationController for the specific cellId.
  3. Animation Step 1 (Fade): Linearly interpolate the fill-opacity of the new faction color from 0.0 to 0.3 over 500ms.
  4. Animation Step 2 (Pulse): Temporarily increase the line-width of the cell's border from 2px to 5px and back to 2px using a Sinusoidal curve.
  5. Refresh the ContiguousBoundaryEngine to recalculate shared edges with adjacent cells.

C. Visibility Toggle (User Story 3)

  1. Listen for the "V" key input or UI button press.
  2. Toggle the isOverlayEnabled state.
  3. Update the Mapbox layer properties:
    // Pseudocode for toggle logic
map.setLayoutProperty('territory-fill-layer', 'visibility', isOverlayEnabled ? 'visible' : 'none');
map.setLayoutProperty('territory-border-layer', 'visibility', isOverlayEnabled ? 'visible' : 'none');

6. Dependencies

  • S2 Geometry Library: Necessary for calculating cell boundaries and neighbor relationships from S2 Tokens.
  • Mapbox GL Expressions: Used for data-driven styling (changing colors based on factionId without re-rendering the whole GeoJSON).
  • Hive DB: Local storage for persisting which cells are conquered while offline.
  • Turf.js (Optional): Can be used for more complex GeoJSON union operations if the Edge Filtering Algorithm becomes too computationally expensive on the main thread.

Depth +1 dynamic loading for seamless cell transitions

▼

User Stories & Criteria

Project: Territory Grids

Feature: Depth +1 Dynamic Loading for Seamless Cell Transitions

This feature focuses on optimizing the user experience during grid navigation by proactively fetching data for adjacent cells. By maintaining a "buffer" of one additional layer of depth (Depth +1), the application ensures that transitions feel instantaneous and data is ready before the user even requests it.

User Story 1: Proactive Neighbor Loading

As a Territory Manager,
I want the system to automatically load all cells immediately adjacent to my current view,
So that I can navigate to neighboring territories without waiting for data to fetch or seeing loading spinners.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Format)

Scenario: Initial load of adjacent cells

  • Given I have successfully logged into the Territory Grid application
  • And I am currently viewing "Cell A" (the focal cell)
  • When the grid initializes
  • Then the system should identify all 8 surrounding cells (the "Depth +1" ring)
  • And trigger a background data fetch for those 8 cells
  • And the UI should remain responsive while these background fetches occur.

Scenario: Updating the buffer upon movement

  • Given I am centered on "Cell A" and all Depth +1 neighbors are loaded
  • When I move my view to "Cell B" (an adjacent cell)
  • Then the system should recalculate the new Depth +1 boundary based on "Cell B"
  • And it should initiate a fetch for any new cells entering the Depth +1 range that are not already in the cache.

User Story 2: Seamless Boundary Transition

As a Power User,
I want the transition between grid cells to be visually fluid,
So that I maintain my sense of orientation and can work across territory borders without interruption.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Format)

Scenario: Transitioning into a pre-loaded cell

  • Given I am viewing "Cell A"
  • And "Cell B" is an adjacent cell that has already been pre-loaded via the Depth +1 logic
  • When I drag the map or use directional keys to move into "Cell B"
  • Then "Cell B" should be rendered immediately with full data visibility
  • And there should be no "Loading..." state or "checkerboard" placeholder visible to the user.

Scenario: Maintaining state during transition

  • Given I am transitioning from "Cell A" to "Cell B"
  • When the center point of my view crosses the boundary into "Cell B"
  • Then the application should promote "Cell B" to the "Primary Cell" status
  • And the UI should update the coordinate/territory labels without a page refresh.

User Story 3: Dynamic Memory Management (Cache Cleanup)

As a System Architect,
I want the application to purge cell data that is no longer within the Depth +1 range,
So that the application's memory usage remains stable during long navigation sessions.

Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Format)

Scenario: Evicting stale cells from cache

  • Given I have moved from "Cell A" to "Cell B"
  • And "Cell X" was a neighbor of "Cell A" but is now "Depth +2" (two cells away) from my current position in "Cell B"
  • When the Depth +1 recalculation is completed
  • Then the system should flag "Cell X" for removal from active memory
  • And release the resources associated with "Cell X" to prevent memory leaks.

Scenario: Re-entry into a purged cell

  • Given "Cell X" was previously purged from memory
  • When I move back toward "Cell X" and it enters the Depth +1 range again
  • Then the system must re-fetch the data for "Cell X" to ensure the information is current.

Technical Specifications

Technical Specification: Depth +1 Dynamic Loading

This specification outlines the implementation of a proactive data-loading layer for the "Territory Grids" project. The system ensures that the player's experience remains uninterrupted by pre-fetching S2 Level 15 cell data for all immediate neighbors of the player's current position.

1. Data Model

The following structure defines the data associated with each individual grid cell. This data is persisted locally in Hive DB and synced with the backend.

Field Type Description
cellId String The unique S2 Level 15 Cell Token (hexadecimal).
centerPoint GeoPoint Latitude and Longitude of the cell's geometric center.
boundaryPoints List List of 4 coordinates defining the S2 cell vertices.
dotBitmask String A bitmask representing the collection status of all programmatic dots in the cell.
totalDots Integer The total count of dots generated for this cell (based on road density).
collectedDots Integer The number of dots currently marked as collected.
status Enum The state of the territory: 'UNEXPLORED', 'IN_PROGRESS', or 'CONQUERED'.
lastUpdated Timestamp The last time the dotBitmask or status was modified.

2. Game State

The application state must track the player's spatial context and the status of the "Buffer Zone" (the Depth +1 ring).

Variable Type Description
focalCellId String The S2 Cell ID currently containing the player's GPS coordinates.
activeBufferIds Set A list of the 8 S2 Cell IDs immediately adjacent to the focalCellId.
cellCache Map<String, CellData> In-memory store of the focal cell and all Depth +1 neighbor data.
loadingQueue List A prioritized queue of Cell IDs currently being fetched from local storage or API.
isTransitioning Boolean Flag indicating if the player is currently crossing a cell boundary.

3. API Endpoints (Local & Remote)

While the MVP prioritizes Hive DB, the system interacts with a data provider service to populate the cells.

Method Endpoint Payload Description
GET /v1/cells/{cellId} N/A Fetches the dot distribution and path data for a specific S2 cell.
POST /v1/cells/batch { cellIds: [] } Fetches data for multiple cells (used for the initial Depth +1 ring).
PUT /v1/cells/{cellId}/sync { dotBitmask: "" } Updates the remote server with local collection progress.

4. Key Components

  • GridManager: Responsible for converting raw GPS coordinates into S2 Level 15 Cell IDs and calculating the 8 neighbors (the "ring").
  • DepthBufferService: Orchestrates the proactive loading. It monitors the focalCellId and triggers fetches for any neighbors not currently in the cellCache.
  • CacheEvictionEngine: Monitors memory usage and removes cell data from cellCache that is no longer within the Depth +1 range.
  • BoundaryObserver: A high-frequency listener that detects when the player's GPS coordinate moves from the focalCellId into one of the activeBufferIds.

5. Logic Flow

A. Initial Load & Buffer Population

  1. Receive initial GPS lock.
  2. GridManager identifies focalCellId.
  3. GridManager identifies 8 neighbors (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) using S2 Geometry library.
  4. DepthBufferService checks cellCache for these 9 IDs.
  5. Missing cells are added to loadingQueue.
  6. CellLoader fetches data from Hive DB (primary) or API (fallback).
  7. UI renders focalCellId immediately; neighbors render in background.

B. Cell Transition (The "Promotion" Logic)

When the player moves:

// Pseudo-algorithm for movement logic
onLocationUpdate(newLocation) {
  String newCellId = S2.tokenFromLocation(newLocation, level: 15);
  
  if (newCellId != focalCellId) {
    // 1. Promote neighbor to Primary
    focalCellId = newCellId;
    
    // 2. Recalculate Buffer
    Set<String> newNeighbors = S2.getNeighbors(newCellId);
    
    // 3. Proactive Fetch
    for (id in newNeighbors) {
      if (!cellCache.contains(id)) {
        loadingQueue.add(id);
        triggerBackgroundFetch(id);
      }
    }
    
    // 4. Cleanup
    triggerEviction(keepIds: [newCellId, ...newNeighbors]);
  }
}

C. Cache Eviction (Memory Management)

To prevent memory leaks during long sessions:

  1. On every focalCellId change, the CacheEvictionEngine scans the cellCache.
  2. Any CellId in the cache that is NOT in the new activeBufferIds or the focalCellId is flagged.
  3. The system disposes of the heavy geometric data (dot coordinates, path arrays) for flagged cells.
  4. The cellId and status may be kept in a lightweight "Summary Map" to speed up re-entry.

6. Dependencies

  • S2 Geometry Library: For high-performance spatial indexing and neighbor calculation.
  • Hive DB: For sub-millisecond local retrieval of cell bitmasks and dot locations.
  • Kalman Filter Service: To ensure GPS jitter doesn't cause "rapid-fire" cell transitions at boundaries.
  • Mapbox GL: For rendering the visual grid overlays and conquered territory polygons.

Technical Design Document (TDD)

▼

1.0 Introduction

▼

The Territory Grids Technical Design Document outlines the architecture for a location-based mobile game where players conquer S2 Level 15 cells by collecting dots. The primary goal is to provide a robust, offline-first experience using Flutter and Mapbox, ensuring high-performance spatial tracking and efficient data persistence.

2.0 System Architecture

▼

The system follows a layered architecture: 1. Presentation Layer (Flutter UI and Mapbox GL integration), 2. Logic Layer (Positioning engine with Kalman filtering, S2 grid controller, and dot generation logic), and 3. Persistence Layer (Hive DB for local storage). The application utilizes a depth +1 loading strategy to pre-fetch adjacent grid data based on the player's current S2 cell.

3.0 Data Models

▼

| Entity | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CellState | s2CellId | String | Unique identifier for the S2 Level 15 grid cell | | CellState | bitmask | String | Hex-encoded string representing the collection status of dots | | CellState | isConquered | Boolean | Indicates if 100% of dots in the cell have been collected | | CellState | lastUpdated | DateTime | Timestamp of the last collection event | | DotObject | position | LatLng | Geographic coordinates of the generated dot | | DotObject | index | Integer | Position of the dot within the cell bitmask |

4.0 API Specification

▼

| Route | Method | Parameters | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | local://grid/getState | GET | cellId | Retrieves the current collection bitmask from Hive DB | | local://grid/update | POST | cellId, dotIndex | Updates the bitmask and checks for conquest completion | | local://map/tiles | GET | bounds | Fetches vector tiles from Mapbox for the specified area |

5.0 Core Feature Implementation

▼

Dots are generated at 15-meter intervals along Mapbox paths (pedestrian, footway, residential) with a 10-meter buffer from intersections and S2 boundaries. | Feature | Mechanism | State Constraint | | --- | --- | --- | | Dot Collection | 4m radius proximity check | Bitmask update | | Conquest | 100% bitmask fill | isConquered = true | | Memory Management | Depth +1 Strategy | Prune cells > 1 distance | Implementation Logic: void processCollection(LatLng playerPos, List dots) { for (var dot in dots) { if (calculateDistance(playerPos, dot.pos) <= 4.0) { markAsCollected(dot.index); } } }

6.0 Deployment & Operations

▼

The application is deployed as a standalone mobile package for iOS and Android. Operations include managing Mapbox API quotas and implementing local storage pruning logic to ensure the Hive DB size remains under 50MB for typical users. Future updates will transition the Hive schema to include ClanMetadata for multiplayer synchronization.

Freelance Briefs

▼

UI/UX Design: Territory Grids Map Interface & Visual Feedback

▼

Brief: UI/UX Design

Project: Territory Grids

Role

UI/UX Designer

Objective
